subject: Immediate: WestUS1 request queue backlog & customer P0 escalation
summary: BrightLeaf reported sustained request queue growth in WestUS1 starting 07:50 PDT; customer-facing latency and 500s increased, multiple routes saturated. We opened a P0 bridge, temporarily steered traffic to WestUS2, and prepared an executive brief for leadership and customer's CTO. Next steps: complete root-cause memory/KV-cache saturation analysis, rollout KV-cache TTL patch, and follow up with credits/contract remediation conversation.

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-07T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + 502s across WestUS1 — joining bridge

Joining bridge. Initial telemetry: 90th/95th tokenization latencies nominal, but request queue length on shard group az-westus1-b is climbing and the per-GPU KV-cache hit ratio dropped ~12% in last 10m. Autoscaler shows no recent scale-up events for that pool (policy threshold is 85% utilization).

Hypothesis: a small (>1M) client prefix storm + large KV load caused the runtime batcher to balloon queue depth and saturate a subset of serving instances. If that's accurate, steering a portion of traffic and forcing a graceful drain should restore tail latency.

I'm preparing a routing plan for ~30% spill to WestUS2, with canary verification. One ask: get authorization from ops/sales to temporarily burst extra dedicated capacity if spill doesn't reduce error rate.

— Jordan (SR oncall)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-07T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Postmortem / exec brief draft + next steps

Team —

Status update for execs and customer: we completed a controlled 30% spill to WestUS2 at 08:42 PDT and provisioned +2 nodes in WestUS1 at 08:53 PDT. Queue depth returned to baseline by 09:05 PDT and 5xxs dropped to nominal. BrightLeaf's ops confirmed latency returned to acceptable range and then we ran a limited traffic ramp for 30 minutes.

Immediate findings: KV-cache churn under a burst of similar prefixes amplified batch formation, causing queue growth on the affected shard group. Root-cause engineering actions: patch to reduce KV cache TTLs for aggressive prefixes and tuning batcher thresholds for variable sequence-length workloads.

Customer / business asks: BrightLeaf requested an executive summary, an incident credit evaluation, and a follow-up engineering session. I've attached the proposed comms draft and a copy of telemetry we used.

Next steps:
- Engineering to ship KV cache TTL patch and tuned batcher config (JIRA OPS-1289) — target 72h
- Customer success to schedule post-incident review with BrightLeaf (Marissa)
- Finance/sales to prepare credit proposal (Vanessa)

I'll queue a postmortem doc and ping leadership. Thanks for the quick response.

— Soojin
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
